text:
sam: kicking off — ran shadow traffic against dedicated pool with int8 AWQ profile, saw both perf spike and a small quality regression on long-seq prompts. leaving raw logs below.

tanya: thanks — quick summary please? :eyes:

sam: short TL;DR:
- workload: mixed Llama-2-70B + Mistral-like variants (tiling + ropescale enabled)
- mode: AWQ int8 runtime kernels (auto selector)
- symptoms: 95th latency doubled for ~10% of requests, and eval set accuracy down ~3.7% vs gptq baseline on our calibration prompts
- repro tag: shadow run id 2026-03-07-ruff

miguel: how long sequences? KV warmup behavior?

sam: mostly long-prefix cases, median seq_out 256 but ~18% > 1024. observed KV-cache cold misses for the first chunk after routing fallback; microtrace attached.

ci-bot: shadow-run 2026-03-07-ruff completed. stash: s3://redwood-shadow/2026-03-07-ruff/logs.tar.gz

ryan: can you paste the kernel selector trace? I want to see when it chose fallback kernels

sam: trace snip:
```
[selector] seq_len=1152 model=mistral14b_awq candidate_kernels=[int8_gemm, fp8_fused, int8_headwise]
[selector] perf_est_ms: int8_gemm=12.1 fp8_fused=9.3 int8_headwise=13.4
[selector] accuracy_risk: int8_gemm=0.02 fp8_fused=0.0 int8_headwise=0.04
[selector] selected=fp8_fused (but runtime used int8_gemm due to device-kernel-mismatch)
[kernel-loader] kernel int8_gemm not resident -> fallback to cpu-cached int8_gemm (latency delta +7.8ms)
[kv] prefix_cache miss for request_id=abcd1234 => full kv rebuild
```

tanya: interesting — so selector predicted fp8_fused but runtime ended up running int8_gemm? mismatch between planner and actual device kernel residency.

miguel: that explains latency. but what about the accuracy regression? fp8->int8 discrepancy?

sam: yes — calibration set shows fp8_fused had 0.6% delta vs gptq, int8_gemm has 4.3% delta. Because selector thought fp8 was chosen, the eval baseline used different quantization expectation. When fallback to int8 happened mid-request the head-scaling + RoPE phase alignment produced subtle token shifts on long prefixes.

anya: do we have the exact eval numbers and prompt set? put them here so SRE or infra can triage.

sam: eval extract:
```
calib_prompts: 500 samples (mix long/short)
baseline(gptq): accuracy=0.912
fp8_fused: accuracy=0.905
int8_gemm: accuracy=0.869
delta(int8_vs_baseline) = -0.043
```

ryan: 4.3% is non-trivial. any repro command so infra can simulate shadow traffic locally? would help to hit kernel residency mismatch.

sam: repro curl (shadow header toggles selector path + forces device kernel cache state):
```
curl -sS -X POST https://staging-infer.redwood/shadow \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $STAGE_KEY" \
  -H "X-Shadow: 1" \
  -d '{"model":"mistral14b_awq","input":"<long-prefix>","seq_out":1200}'
```

miguel: can we fix by making selector check kernel residency before committing selection? e.g., require kernel_resident=true or plan a warmup load.

tanya: proposal:
- selector do preflight: kernel_resident check (fast) and prefer resident kernels when perf delta < 1.5x
- on model rollout config, add small warmup traffic to bind kernels for known long-seq hot models
- if runtime fallback occurs, trigger a quick fallback-quality check and opt for fp8 path if accuracy impact predicted > 2%

sam: also add KV cache heuristics: when route changes mid-request, avoid full KV rebuild if prefix fingerprint matches within first 128 tokens. That reduces cold-miss penalty.

ryan: agree. short term: patch selector to prefer resident kernel when seq_len>512 and perf_est delta < 20%. Long-term: add kernel residency signals to per-route console metrics.

ci-bot: created issue #INF-9243: "kernel-residency aware selector + kv-fingerprint warmup" assigned to eng-runtime.

anya: does this suggest we should prefer fp8 for long sequences to avoid head-scale/ropes issues? fp8 accuracy looked close to baseline.

sam: fp8 is promising for these cases — lower accuracy delta and lower perf. but AWQ for other models still better in token quality in some short-prefix settings. we should per-model-profile these rules.

miguel: next steps:
1) small patch to selector (resident check) + hotload during canary
2) add shadow warmup traffic for long-seq heavy customers for 72h
3) add a nightly calibration run comparing AWQ/GPTQ/FP8 on 1k synthetic long prompts

tanya: I'll spin up the PR for selector changes and test harness. tagging @ryan for infra changes.

ryan: will add kernel residency exporter and a one-off cron to pre-warm kernels on dedicated pools.

sam: thanks — filing the short reproduction logs in the bug. will follow up with a trimmed packet of the worst 50 repro requests.

miguel: :thumbsup: 

ci-bot: linked INF-9243 -> epic INF-9000 (runtime stability).
